description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, celebrated for its crispy edges and tender interior packed with fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This authentic recipe guides you to create a delightful culinary experience, perfect as an appetizer or a light meal. Enjoy the rich flavors and satisfying texture that make this dish a Korean favorite.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, and gochugaru (if using). Stir well and set aside. This sauce will complement the rich flavors of your Haemul Pajeon.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Clean and chop the shrimp and squid into bite-sized pieces. If using other seafood like mussels or clams, prepare them accordingly. Slice the green onions into 3-4 inch lengths, and thinly slice the yellow onion and red chili (if desired).

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour, salt, cold water, and the large egg until just combined. It's important not to overmix the batter; a few small lumps are perfectly fine and contribute to a tender pancake.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the prepared shrimp, squid, sliced green onions, yellow onion, and red chili (if using) into the batter. Gently fold the ingredients together until they are evenly coated with the batter. This ensures a good distribution of flavors in every bite.

instructions.title: Cook the First Pancake
instructions.text: Heat 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Pour about one-quarter of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it evenly with a spatula to form a thin, round pancake. You can arrange some extra green onion pieces on top for a beautiful presentation.

instructions.title: Flip and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Cook the pancake for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula and cook for another 3-4 minutes on the other side until it's also golden, crispy, and the seafood is thoroughly cooked through. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice it into wedges or squares and serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat the cooking process with the remaining batter, adding more oil to the pan as needed for each subsequent pancake. Enjoy the fresh, savory goodness!

tips: For the crispiest Haemul Pajeon, use very cold water for your batter and include rice flour. Avoid overmixing the batter, as this can develop gluten and make the pancake chewy instead of tender.

Feel free to customize your pajeon with your favorite seafood such as mussels, clams, or oysters. Ensure all seafood is fresh and well-drained before adding it to the batter to prevent a soggy pancake.

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed immediately after cooking while it's still hot and crispy. Serve it fresh with the dipping sauce, perhaps alongside a bottle of chilled makgeolli (Korean rice wine) for an authentic experience.
article:
Dive into the vibrant world of Korean cuisine, and you’ll quickly discover a dish that perfectly encapsulates its diverse flavors and textures: Haemul Pajeon. More than just a pancake, this savory delight is a culinary experience, offering a symphony of fresh seafood, crisp green onions, and a perfectly golden-brown, often crispy, batter. Whether you’re a seasoned fan of Korean food or just beginning your exploration, Haemul Pajeon is a must-try – a dish that brings comfort, flavor, and a touch of the sea to your table.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon, often simply called Korean seafood pancake, is a popular savory pancake dish from Korea. The name itself provides a clue to its main components: “Haemul” means seafood, and “Pajeon” refers to a scallion (or green onion) pancake. Unlike sweet dessert pancakes, Haemul Pajeon is savory, packed with an abundance of fresh seafood like shrimp, squid, and mussels, combined with plenty of thinly sliced green onions, all bound together in a light, flavorful batter. It’s typically pan-fried until golden and crispy on the outside, while remaining tender and moist on the inside. This dish is particularly beloved on rainy days in Korea, often enjoyed with a refreshing glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine), creating a cozy and comforting experience. Its appeal lies in its textural contrast and the fresh, briny flavors of the sea mingling with the subtle sweetness of the scallions.

## Ingredients for Haemul Pajeon

Creating an authentic Haemul Pajeon starts with selecting the right ingredients. Here’s a breakdown of what you’ll typically need:

For the Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour (or a mix of all-purpose and glutinous rice flour for extra chewiness)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1/4 teaspoon black pepper
*   1 cup cold water (or ice water for a crispier result)
*   1 large egg (optional, for richness)

For the Filling:
*   1/2 lb mixed seafood (shrimp, squid rings, mussels, oysters – cleaned and chopped into bite-sized pieces)
*   1 bunch green onions (about 8-10 stalks), cut into 2-3 inch lengths
*   1/2 small onion, thinly sliced (optional)
*   1 small red chili, thinly sliced (optional, for a touch of heat and color)

For Cooking:
*   Vegetable oil (or any neutral cooking oil)

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
*   1 clove garlic, minced
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds

## How to Make Haemul Pajeon: Step-by-Step

Making Haemul Pajeon is a straightforward process that yields incredibly delicious results. Follow these steps for a perfect pancake:

Step 1: Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables
Thoroughly clean your mixed seafood. If using shrimp, peel and devein them. Cut larger pieces of squid or shrimp into bite-sized chunks. Pat all seafood dry with paper towels to prevent the batter from becoming watery. Wash and trim the green onions, then cut them into roughly 2-3 inch pieces. If using, thinly slice the onion and red chili.

Step 2: Make the Batter
In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, salt, and black pepper. Gradually add the cold water (and egg, if using), whisking continuously until you have a smooth batter with no lumps. The consistency should be similar to a thin pancake batter, slightly thinner than regular American pancake batter. Using cold water helps create a crisper exterior.

Step 3: Combine Ingredients
Add the prepared seafood, green onions, and any other sliced vegetables (onion, chili) directly into the batter. Gently mix until everything is evenly coated. Be careful not to overmix, as this can develop the gluten in the flour and make the pancake tough.

Step 4: Pan-Fry the Pancake
Heat a large, non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a generous amount of vegetable oil (about 2-3 tablespoons) to coat the bottom of the pan. Once the oil is hot and shimmering, pour about half of the batter mixture into the pan, spreading it out evenly to form a large, round pancake. You want it to be about 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick. For a more traditional look, arrange some of the green onion pieces artistically on top before the batter sets.

Cook for 5-7 minutes on the first side, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, and the edges start to look cooked through. You can carefully lift an edge with a spatula to check the color.

Step 5: Flip and Finish Cooking
Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula (or two spatulas for larger pancakes). You might need to add a little more oil around the edges of the pan to ensure even crisping. Cook for another 4-6 minutes on the second side, pressing down gently with your spatula to ensure good contact with the pan and encourage crispiness. The Haemul Pajeon is done when both sides are golden brown and the seafood is cooked through.

Step 6: Serve
Carefully slide the cooked Haemul Pajeon onto a cutting board. Cut it into wedges, like a pizza, or into squares. Serve immediately while hot.

## Tips for the Best Crispy Haemul Pajeon

The hallmark of an excellent Haemul Pajeon is its crispy exterior. Achieving this perfect crunch requires a few key techniques:

*   **Cold Batter:** Use ice-cold water (or even a few ice cubes) in your batter. The temperature difference between the cold batter and hot oil creates steam, resulting in a lighter, crispier texture.
*   **Don't Overmix:** Overmixing develops gluten, which can lead to a tougher pancake. Mix just enough to combine the ingredients.
*   **Plenty of Oil:** Don’t be shy with the oil. A generous amount of hot oil is crucial for achieving that desirable crispy crust. Think shallow-frying rather than just pan-frying.
*   **High Heat (Initially):** Start with medium-high heat to quickly crisp the exterior, then you can reduce it slightly to ensure the inside cooks through without burning the outside.
*   **Press Down:** After flipping, gently press down on the pancake with your spatula. This ensures maximum contact with the hot pan, promoting even browning and crispiness.
*   **Rice Flour or Cornstarch:** For an extra crispy bite, consider substituting 1/4 cup of the all-purpose flour with glutinous rice flour (chapssalgaru) or cornstarch. This helps create a lighter, more delicate crisp.
*   **Cook One at a Time:** If making large pancakes, cook one at a time to maintain consistent heat and prevent the pan from becoming overcrowded, which can steam the pancake rather than crisp it.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed fresh off the pan, while it’s still warm and crispy. Cut it into bite-sized wedges or squares and serve it as an appetizer, a side dish, or even a light meal.

The accompanying dipping sauce is essential and easy to make. Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, minced garlic, gochugaru, and toasted sesame seeds. This tangy, savory, and slightly spicy sauce perfectly complements the rich flavors of the pancake. You can also add a pinch of sugar or finely chopped green onions to the sauce for extra flavor.

Traditionally, Haemul Pajeon pairs wonderfully with makgeolli, the milky, slightly fizzy Korean rice wine. Its subtle sweetness and effervescence cut through the richness of the pancake, making for a truly authentic Korean dining experience. It also goes well with soju or a cold beer.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is fantastic on its own, there are many ways to customize it to your taste or dietary needs:

*   **Different Seafood:** Feel free to experiment with other types of seafood. Oysters, clams, or even a mix including imitation crab meat can be delicious additions.
*   **Add Vegetables:** Enhance the vegetable content by adding thinly sliced carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, or even a handful of chopped kimchi for a spicy kick (Kimchi Pajeon is another popular variation!).
*   **Meat Options:** While traditionally seafood, some variations include thinly sliced beef (e.g., bulgogi meat) or pork for a heartier pancake.
*   **Vegetarian Pajeon:** For a vegetarian option, simply omit the seafood and increase the amount of green onions and other vegetables like mushrooms (e.g., Beoseot Pajeon). You can also add crumbled firm tofu for extra protein.
*   **Egg Wash:** For an extra rich and slightly thicker pancake, some recipes call for pouring a whisked egg over the top of the pancake just before flipping, allowing it to set and create a beautiful golden crust.

No matter how you prepare it, Haemul Pajeon remains a delightful and satisfying dish. Its versatility and comforting flavors make it a beloved staple in Korean cuisine, perfect for sharing with friends and family. So next time you're craving something savory, crispy, and full of flavor, give this Korean seafood pancake a try!
